findings.reason: adding `sn-definitions-by-construction#s11` to s3's depends-on is what stops that node being dispatched ahead of the mechanism the bar checks.
findings.text: §3 requires the release cut to refuse when a member's shared wording is not the rendering of its stored sentence, which is exactly the capability `sn-definitions-by-construction#s11` delivers, but the section-declaration map gives s3 only `sn-audited-group-release#s1`; a node dispatched on s3 would be asked to gate on machinery another plan has not yet built and would report the refusal as unproducible

findings.reason: one line naming which reading the bar gates on and requiring the after-rate audit turns a release gate that a repaired group cannot pass into a checkable one.
findings.text: the bar's refusal condition is "the group's audited defect rate is above the ruled bar or was never measured", and §4 audits each group member once, before repair; §4 and §5 then require the release notes to state the after rate, so either the cut is gated on a rate the repair has invalidated or the after rate is reported with no audit that produces it

findings.reason: naming where the planted labels come from (independently built fixtures versus the very labels the note distrusts) decides whether the control measures the readers or merely repeats the old label set.
findings.text: §1's negative control plants "twenty names known to be defective and twenty known to be sound", but the section's own premise is that neither the review score nor the stored label set measures correctness, and no provenance for those forty labels is named; the readers' recall and false-alarm rates therefore rest on ground truth the section has just argued does not exist

findings.reason: the sample floor decides whether §2's ranking and §4's first-group choice rest on a measurable quantity or on an interval too wide to order anything.
findings.text: the stratified sample is "at least 150" over every group of twenty or more live names, and the graph holds 23 such groups, so each contributes ~6-7 names, while §2 (line 33) requires "the count the audit of §1 reads as wrong-domain with its interval" per group and §4 ranks groups on that reading; at n≈7 an interval spans tens of percentage points and cannot separate groups at 88-96% agreement

findings.reason: naming one durable evidence location makes §3's refusals and §5's table review at all, and it is the only way the done-whens can be checked after the nodes end.
findings.text: every section hands its result to "the evidence" or to "a recorded run" (§3's planted-fault refusals, §5's one group-by-group table) and the plan never names the path those live on, so a later reader has nothing to open and a node can satisfy the wording with a scratchpad

findings.reason: the plan currently locks the first group before the ranking exists, so a lead ruling that orders any other group first contradicts §4 outright and leaves §5 to re-do it.
findings.text: §4 asserts "The first group is the one §2 ranks best defined; on today's reading that is equilibrium (210 live names, 200 with a domain among their sources')", but §2 measures agreement as a ratio and its own quoted numbers put spectroscopy (50 of 52, 96%) and magnetic field systems (121 of 126, 96%) above equilibrium (200 of 210, 95%), while §2's done-when defers the order to the lead and requires "the measure used stated"; the section therefore fixes a choice §2 has not made, on a measure §2 has not fixed
